newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish lower on US rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish lower on US rate hike fears.

text.p: French shares finished lower on Tuesday reversing their gains in late trade as rate hike fears in the United States drove Wall Street lower, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.33 points or 0.26 percent at 2,080.86 while the CAC-40 September futures contract closed down 3.5 points at 2,089.0. Volume was a heavy 5.7 billion francs.
The bourse had moved in positive territory in early afternoon trade and managed to hold its slight gains after the release of U.S. economic statistics for August.
U.S. industrial output rose 0.5 percent in August and capacity utilisation increased to 83.5 percent.
"U.S data were broadly in line with market expectations. But the Fed news really hit the market," one dealer said.
A majority of district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a hike in the 5.0 percent discount rate, a senior Fed official said on Tuesday.

LVMH lost 3.09 percent, falling to 1130.0 francs, after unit Hermes reported a weaker first half operating profit. Brokeragee SGE Delahaye cut its rating on Hermes to under-perform from neutral and lowered its earnings estimates.

Michelin gained 1.96 percent to 265.20 francs on news of a 50 percent jump in first half profit excluding exceptionals to 2.88 billion francs. Broker Cheuvreux de Virieu also included Michelin in its list of recommended stocks.
